title: First dance in Wilmington: Dizzy as straw boss and head arrangements
summary: Dizzy runs the band, calling blues choruses for Malachi and riffs for the sections, and Eckstine asks all writers for charts.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Anyway, we went down, and we started the dance off that night with Dizzy... Dizzy was the straw boss of the band. he used to rehearse the band. So he'd come over to the piano and tell me to play a couple of choruses of the Blues, and he'd give me a tempo, and I'd play a couple of choruses, or as many

choruses as I wanted, and then perhaps him or one of the trumpet players, or a trombone player would start...take a solo, and the saxes would play some sort of riff or rhythm behind them that Charlie Parker had told them to play. Sometimes both sides would...it would be a unison thing. Then after they'd play a few choruses, one of the saxophone players would get up and the brass would play something, and it would be something that Dizzy told them to play. He would start off playing it, and they'd just fall in.

Anyway, all night we played, and it was a joy. It was just like playing in a jam session. The only thing, guys were playing things together, you know. So in the meantime, Billy Eckstine, he asked everyone in the band who could write, to write an arrangement, so we could get some music together right away.
